hints.title: Prefix Tree Root Replacement
hints.text: Every word in the sentence should be replaced by the shortest root in the dictionary that forms its prefix. How can a prefix tree expedite prefix lookup?

hints.title: Shortest Prefix Termination Invariant
hints.text: When traversing characters of a word in the prefix tree, stopping at the very first terminal root node guarantees the shortest replacement.

hints.title: Prefix Search and Sentence Reassembly Procedure
hints.text: Insert all dictionary words into a prefix tree where end nodes mark root completion. Split the sentence into words. For each word, walk down the tree branch by branch. If a root end marker is reached, substitute the word with that root; if a branch breaks, retain the original word. Join words with spaces.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input length or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N + W) time and O(D) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing every sentence word against every dictionary root requires O(W * D * L) operations, leading to excessive string comparisons.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The prefix tree indexes all roots in O(total root characters) space, resolving each word lookup in linear time relative to word length.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should construct a trie and exit early at the first matching prefix marker to ensure minimal replacement length.
